scope: Read-only independent review of six fixture files and production Cancel/transition contracts. Author offline logs independently recounted; retained original inputs and binary hashes read-only rechecked. No Go test, PostgreSQL query/write, Docker query/mutation, service, mount, key read, or acceptance execution was performed in this review.

original_retained_inputs.database_route: exact restricted original role/private schema/loopback validated without disclosing credential

reviewed_boundaries: A dedicated fixture control flock serializes abort and new SIGTERM entry. It neither creates nor rebinds pool owners. Fresh physical preflight requires exact verified slots, no owner, empty engine/artifacts and absent journal/WAL/SHM/socket before any abort or new schema/process.

Original authority binds current/archived acceptance, old executable bytes, recovery phase/run/schema/role/config hashes, private credential route, fixture source and original read-only audit. Original PID/config/binary processes and original-run managed Docker containers are rejected by runtime read-only checks.

Before observation uses repeatable-read and requires the original queued v1/no lease/no workspace/single run and zero work/fee/capacity. Only production Store.Cancel persists the control transition; no SQL state, deadline, lease, migration or synthetic receipt shortcut exists.

After oracle requires cancel_requested v2/terminal=false/target cancelled, exactly one pending stop command and one seq0 initialize committed empty-input/output control step. All model/effect/allocation/quota/artifact/cleanup/message/approval work remains zero; immutable run columns and original event/snapshot rows remain equal.

Exclusive durable intent permits explicit same-intent observation after an ambiguous Cancel result, preserving old evidence. An existing report is revalidated against current database history without repeating the transaction. Partial malformed evidence fails closed.

Attempt02 requires its exact manifest and new revision binary directory. Before new schema/process it revalidates old abort against live restricted original PG. New evidence/private paths, schema, role and run are separate; children receive only new worker credentials. At completion old database/history is revalidated again after new worker and runner exit.

Recovery and S12 L5 derive private paths from the selected SIGTERM attempt. L5 compares archived manifest/binary/config/process/claim evidence against the selected sigterm02 schema. Earlier lifecycle assertions, default lease and production cleanup remain unchanged.
limits: No actual abort or SIGTERM success is established by this review. Final execution still requires the new binary build attestation and the runtime live checks, followed by raw evidence audit.
The original nonterminal cancel_requested run remains schedulable; retain its schema without any worker. Fixture abandonment does not claim terminal business cancellation or journal recovery.

Read-only database transactions and filesystem/process/Docker checks are separate observations, not atomic cross-system proof. The private operator scope must remain quiescent; the fixture flock does not fence an unrelated manually launched worker.
Historical audit counts are not substituted for live checks. This report did not reconnect to PostgreSQL or resample daemon/process identities.
Original control-step count is one after Cancel, while snapshot step_seq and effect/model execution remain zero.
